stem: Insects are often (i)____ as the world's most versatile and (ii)____ flying machines. Yet they shouldn't even be able to get off the ground, at least not according to a straightforward interpretation of the laws of aerodynamics.

Predators try to (i)____ their ultimate energy intake by (ii)____ the effort they expend searching for and handling prey relative to the energy the prey provides. Thus, a particular kind of prey would be (iii)____ to a predator's diet only if it is worth the predator's time and energy—that is, if it increases the animal's overall energy profit during foraging.

The term "borderline, coined in the 1930s to describe a psychiatric condition straddling the boundary between two other diagnoses, remained ____ until John Gunderson enumerated six identifying characteristics of the condition in the 1970s.
In this otherwise ____ study, the internal tensions resulting from the increasing integration of the United States with the world economy are simply mentioned rather than analyzed.

Although Ralph Ellison's Invisible Man has been heavily praised for over 50 years by a wide variety of critics and scholars, there have been ____ from the outset concerning the novel’s political vision.

Egler's prediction in 1947 that the introduction of mangrove trees to the Hawaiian lslands would cause sweeping ecological change was ____: extensive mangrove forests have come to displace many preexisting plant communities.
